title: The mystery box
_map: Your senses (Y1). Big idea: five senses and the body parts that sense them. Creative: mystery boxes: work out what's inside without looking.
_story: Steve only has eyes and wonders how people know so much about the world. Ismaeel matches each sense to its body part, then plays the mystery box game for real.
_stepChain: you find out about the world → seeing (eyes), hearing (ears), touching (skin, hands), smelling (nose), tasting (tongue) → each is called a sense → Steve can only see → a mystery box uses the other senses

talk.goodAnswer: seeing, hearing, touching, smelling and tasting.

talk.ask: In the mystery box game, which senses did you use?
talk.goodAnswer: touch, hearing, and maybe smell. Not sight!

handsOn: Mystery box! A grown-up hides something in a bag or box. Without looking, use touch, sound and smell to guess what it is. Then swap.

narration.speaker: steve
narration.text: Ismaeel, how do you find out about the world? In my game, I mostly look around. But you can find out so much more! How?
You see with your eyes. Blink blink! You hear with your ears. And you feel things with your skin, especially your fingers! Each way of finding out about the world is called a sense.
There are two more! Smelling, with your nose. Sniff sniff! And tasting, with your tongue. Yum!

question.prompt: How many senses is that altogether?
question.onRight: Yes! Seeing, hearing, touching, smelling and tasting. 5 senses!

0.say: Seeing, hearing, touching: that's 3. Add smelling and tasting: 5 senses!

2.mistake: counted fingers or body parts, not senses
2.hint: Count each one on your fingers: see, hear, touch, smell, taste.
2.say: Count each sense on your fingers: seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, tasting. That's 5!

narration.speaker: steve
narration.text: Here's a game where you can't use your eyes: the mystery box! Feel it. Shake it, and listen. Sniff it! Can you guess what's inside? Play it with a grown-up!

rule.text: 5 senses: see, hear, touch, smell, taste.
rule.ask: Can you say your five senses? Say them out loud! Then tap the eye.
rule.spoken: We have five senses: seeing with our eyes, hearing with our ears, touching with our skin, smelling with our nose, and tasting with our tongue.

bonus.prompt: Bonus! Why does food taste of less when you have a blocked nose?
bonus.reveal: Smell and taste work as a team! Lots of what we call taste is really smell.
